records.answer: Your DevOps team needs to set up a network path from the control plane to your API server and create a cross-account IAM role. Additionally, your cluster admin needs to set up Kubernetes RBAC for that role. You also need to create a namespace before you start. You can create the namespace using the command `kubectl create namespace <namespace>`. Your DevOps team should also have the cluster name and the AWS account id of the node group, which is not always the account the cluster is in.

records.answer: You can set the shared API key at the team scope, this way all team members will inherit the team default. However, be aware that setting a value at user scope overrides team and tenant for your sessions only. Also, note that personal credentials should always be set at user scope and not at team scope, as it overwrites your teammates. To set the API key at team scope, follow the secret resolution order: user → team → tenant, with the first match winning.

records.answer: You can run a session with the Cursor runtime, but if your workspace declares `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, it will still demand Claude credentials. To avoid this, you can either supply the token or use a workspace that does not declare it. Selecting a runtime does not change what the workspace requires, so a workspace that declares `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` will still demand it even on a Cursor run. You can use `CURSOR_API_KEY` instead if you do not have Claude access.

records.answer: You have a situation where the CLI and the MCP are authenticating independently and resolving to different tenants. This is not necessarily a fault, as they do not share a credential. The MCP is what your agent uses, so it's worth settling this before dispatching anything. To tell them apart, look for the token rather than guessing. You can run `auth/whoami` on both surfaces and compare. If the tenant the MCP reports is not in the list of tokens, no configuration is producing it and you are looking at a cached connection: restart the editor. If it is in the list, that is the separate-credential case. Regenerate the key from the tenant you want and update the MCP registration. Also, if your API key is rejected, the server was reached and your key was rejected, see the troubleshooting guide for credentials and keys.

To set a team-scoped secret, go to the web UI → Secrets → Add secret → scope **team**. This way, all team members will inherit the team default, and you can control what they can do with grants.

records.answer: The CLI and the MCP authenticate independently and can resolve to different tenants. The MCP is what your agent uses, so settle this before dispatching anything. Two different situations can produce this symptom: separate credentials or a stale connection. Check if a token for the reported tenant exists in your config. If it does, regenerate the key from the tenant you want and update the MCP registration. If it doesn't, fully restart your editor. You can verify the key with `auth/whoami` and check the response to see if the key is good. If the key is rejected, get a new API key from Settings → API Keys → Create key, and update your MCP configuration with it.
